objective: Resolve the reviewed Docker seccomp SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ operand order with an applied-profile guest probe.

finding.review_disposition: P0 rejected: the reviewed claim that 1/15 cannot match is empirically false and omits libseccomp's datum mask fixup.
finding.corrected_severity: P1 policy precision: 1/15 admits odd base socket types to the kernel; this probe observed no successful unintended socket and does not establish authority expansion.
finding.conclusion: The production 1/15 rule admits AF_INET SOCK_STREAM with protocol 0, including SOCK_CLOEXEC. It also lets SOCK_RAW protocol 0 reach the kernel, which returns EPROTONOSUPPORT. The tightened 15/1 rule preserves both STREAM cases and rejects RAW with the profile's EPERM; both profiles reject DGRAM and protocol 255.
finding.semantics: libseccomp treats value as the mask and valueTwo as the datum, then masks the datum before emitting BPF. Thus 1/15 becomes (type & 1) == (15 & 1), while 15/1 becomes (type & 15) == (1 & 15).

runtime.qualification_note: runc applies the profile; the guest libseccomp package is recorded as image provenance and is not the library that constructs the host-side filter.

filter_builder_versions.host_libseccomp: not exposed by Docker inspect/version; semantics were verified through the applied filter rather than inferred from the guest package

primary_sources.claim: Pinned libseccomp 2.5.4 maps datum_a to mask and datum_b to datum, then masks the datum before BPF generation.
libseccomp-golang documents MakeCondition operand handling and masked equality.
runc passes config Arg.Value and Arg.ValueTwo to libseccomp MakeCondition in that order.

controls.probe_compilation: Fixed source embedded in this script, compiled inside the approved guest into a disposable Docker-managed volume.
controls.compiler_user: 0:0 with every capability dropped; probe execution user is 65534:65534
controls.profile_difference: Only socket argument 1 value/valueTwo changed from 1/15 to 15/1 in the corrected temporary copy.
